figures.title: One lane, read and written at every block
figures.caption: Every sublayer reads the residual stream, computes a correction, and adds it back. The lane holds one vector per token at width d_model from the embedding lookup to the unembedding; attention and the feed-forward network never replace it, so nothing else survives the depth.
figures.alt: A left-to-right lane of five stages: embedding, attention, feed-forward, final norm, and unembedding, each labelled with its width, d_model except the unembedding's V. Above the stages a bypass line labelled residual stream runs the whole length, showing that the original vector is added back past every stage rather than replaced.

data.bypass: residual stream: width d_model, never replaced
data.note: Attention is the only stage that moves information between positions; every other stage is per-token. Encoder layers write to the stream twice, decoder layers three times.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to add each write to the lane.

steps.label: The embedding lookup writes the first vector into the lane.
Attention reads the lane at every position and adds its output back.
The feed-forward network reads and writes one position at a time.
The final norm rescales the accumulated stream.
The unembedding scores every vocabulary item from the same lane.

figures.title: Where the norm sits decides what the identity path carries
figures.caption: Post-norm puts LayerNorm after the addition, so the norm's Jacobian multiplies the identity term and rescaling sits directly in the gradient path. Pre-norm normalizes only the sublayer branch, leaving a bare identity term; that is why it trains without warmup, and why the stream's norm is never renormalized and grows with depth.
figures.alt: Two panels. Post-norm: y equals LayerNorm of x plus F of x; the Jacobian is J_N plus J_N J_F; the norm multiplies the identity term; the stream is renormalized every layer and practice used learning-rate warmup. Pre-norm: y equals x plus F of LayerNorm of x; the Jacobian is I plus J_F J_N; the identity term is a bare I; the stream is never renormalized, so L independent writes of variance v give variance Lv and standard deviation square root of Lv.

panels.title: post-norm (2017 paper)
items: the norm multiplies the identity term
panels.note: Magnitude stays bounded, but rescaling sits directly in the identity path.

panels.title: pre-norm (GPT-2, GPT-3, LLaMA)
items: the identity term is a bare I
panels.note: The stream's norm grows with depth: L independent writes of variance v give variance Lv and standard deviation sqrt(Lv).

sources.note: He et al. 2016, ResNet: the identity path and the degradation problem.
Xiong et al. 2020: pre-norm versus post-norm gradients and the warmup argument.
Wang et al. 2022, DeepNet/DeepNorm: scaling the residual and sublayer initialization for post-norm depth.
Elhage et al. 2022, Toy Models of Superposition: fixed-width interference between features.
nostalgebraist 2020: applying the final norm and unembedding to intermediate streams.
Belrose et al. 2023, the tuned lens: per-layer affine maps before the unembedding.
